subject: geography
title: Water: Lesotho Highlands Case Study

concepts.def: Small mountainous country surrounded by South Africa.
Lesotho Highlands Water Project, large-scale water transfer to RSA.
185 m high concrete arch dam, the project's largest reservoir.
Hydroelectric power generated at Muela meets most of Lesotho needs.
Water royalties supply around 10% of Lesotho's GDP.
Around 30,000 people displaced from flooded valleys. ⛰

walkthroughs.body_html:
Lesotho is high, wet and water-rich.

Its giant neighbour South Africa is drier and densely industrial.

The LHWP transfers water north-west to Gauteng.

The scheme is huge.

Katse Dam rises 185 m; water flows through long tunnels to the Vaal system.

At Muela the water also generates HEP for Lesotho.

Benefits vs costs.

Royalties add ~10% to Lesotho's GDP and clean water flows to RSA cities.

Roughly 30,000 people were displaced and downstream ecosystems harmed.
